method: Reviewed full draft against Korea Energy Agency min24 winter heating guidance (indoor temperature rise of about 2-3C from bubble wrap, curtains and draft stoppers, 20C setpoint, 7% saving per 1C, 5-10 minute ventilation), Ministry policy briefing pages (window heat loss share 30% cited from the former Ministry of Land; 40-60% humidity, condensation and mold prevention), the BECC window U-value explainer (window frames conduct heat at least 7x faster than walls, up to 20% heating cost difference), the MOLIT energy saving design standard annex 4 U-value table (single glazing 6.6, double low-E 1.9-3.5, triple 1.5-2.8 W/m2K) and the SBS field test quoting the Korea Conformity Laboratories (bubble wrap room 9.2C vs 7.0C after one hour, 2.2C difference; draft stopper 7.2C, storm film 7.7C). Film certification criteria (visible light transmittance >=50%, solar heat gain <=0.5) come from the KEA high-efficiency appliance registry. All numbers in the draft are covered by the research record.
